variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal names one cube color (red, blue or green); call it the goal cube. The goal also says whether the wanted target is the one used 'before' or 'after' the button press; honour that word when computing goal_target. Never choose C (press the button): the button press in the video is only a marker telling you which target to use. Rules, applied in whatever situation you stand in: 1. Start of episode (memory empty, goal_target unknown, gripper raised out of frame, fingers 100% open): read the goal for 'before' or 'after', compute goal_target from the demonstration as the memory instruction says, then choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the goal cube's current position in the execution scene. e.g. A: pick up the cube at [84, 122]. 2. Cube in hand (the scene at this decision step shows fingers about 46% open with the gripper raised, height near 0.15, after the execution steps showed it descend to the cube and close; the cube may or may not be reported as 'held in the gripper', trust the finger opening) and cube_placed is 'no': choose B: drop onto, pointing at the target entry in the current scene nearest to goal_target (targets wobble a few pixels; use the current listed position, e.g. B: drop onto at [87, 101]). If no listed target is within 10 pixels of goal_target (it may be hidden), point at goal_target itself. 3. Cube not in hand (fingers 100% open) and cube_placed is 'no' and goal_target is known: the pick failed or was never done; choose A: pick up the cube at the goal cube's current position. 4. cube_placed is 'yes' and the goal cube rests on goal_target: the task is complete; if a subgoal is still required, choose B: drop onto the same target again only if the cube is in hand, otherwise choose A: pick up the goal cube (keeps the loop safe). Never press the button. 5. Any situation not covered: if fingers are about 46% open and the gripper is raised, treat the cube as held and apply rule 2; otherwise apply rule 3. Never choose C.

fields.name: goal_target
fields.description: If the memory carried in holds a value, copy it unchanged. If it is empty (first step, demonstration shown): read the goal instruction and note whether it says 'before' or 'after' the button was pressed. In the demonstration steps find the press frame: the first frame with fingers 0% open and height under 0.05, gripper over the button. A release is a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to 88% or more while height is under 0.05. For 'before', take the last release earlier than the press frame; for 'after', take the first release later than the press frame (do not take the later put-away release, where the cube ends more than 8 px from any target). The goal cube's [y, x] in that release frame is the placement point. Among the target entries listed in the execution scene at the bottom of this step, write the [y, x] of the one nearest that point. e.g. [86, 100]
fields.annotation: The [y, x] of the target the goal instruction names: the one the demonstration placed the goal cube on right before the button press if the goal says 'before', or right after it if the goal says 'after'. Found by reading the whole demonstration. The press frame is the first demonstration frame where the fingers go to 0% open with height under 0.05 and the gripper over the button. A release is a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to 88% or more with height under 0.05. If the goal says 'before', take the last release earlier than the press frame; if it says 'after', take the first release later than the press frame (a later put-away release, where the cube ends more than 8 px from every target, is ignored). The goal cube's position in that release frame is the placement point; the field holds the [y, x] of the target entry nearest that point as listed in the scene at the start of execution. Written at the first decision step and never changed afterwards. e.g. [86, 100]

history.critique:
field goal_target, ANNOTATOR PROMPT
  Replaces target_before_button. The goal instruction varies: it names the target the demonstration used either 'right before' or 'right after' the button was pressed, and the old field always took the before-placement, so on an 'after' goal the policy carried the wrong target and dropped the cube on the before-target (SUFFICIENCY fails at the drop step: the correct target is nowhere in memory and the demonstration is no longer visible). In every demonstration the pattern is the same: the goal cube is picked and released on one target, the gripper closes to 0% and descends low over the button (the press), the cube is picked again and released on a second target, then it is picked once more and released at a spot that is not on any target (a put-away). New filling: find the press frame (fingers 0%, height under 0.05, gripper over the button). A release is a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to 88% or more with height under 0.05. If the goal says 'before', take the last release before the press frame; if the goal says 'after', take the first release after the press frame (the put-away release later is ignored because the cube there lies more than 8 px from every target). The cube's position in the release frame is the placement point; the field holds the [y, x] of the target entry in the scene at the start of execution nearest that point. Written at the first decision step, unchanged afterwards. e.g. [86, 100]

the policy prompt for subgoal
  Rule 1 sent the policy wrong on an 'after' goal: it told the policy to compute the before-button target regardless of the goal wording. Replace it with: at the start of the episode (memory empty, gripper raised out of frame, fingers 100% open) read the goal for 'before' or 'after', compute goal_target as the memory instruction says, then choose A: pick up the cube at the goal cube's current position. Rule 2 and rule 4 should refer to goal_target instead of target_before_button: with the cube in hand (fingers ~46% open, gripper raised near height 0.15, after the execution steps showed a descent and closing on the cube; the 'held in the gripper' note may be absent) and cube_placed 'no', choose B: drop onto, pointing at the listed target in the current scene nearest goal_target (within 10 px; if none is listed that close, point at goal_target itself). Rule 3 and rule 5 stay as they are. Add one sentence to the preamble: the goal may name any cube color (red, blue or green) and may say 'before' or 'after' the button press; both words are to be honoured, and the button itself is still never pressed.

refused
  One drop step on a 'before' goal reported that the memory should have held the target the demonstration used after the button press, and asked for a 'more robust' recipe to get there. In that demonstration the cube was unmistakably released on one target, the button was then pressed, and only afterwards was the cube released on the second target, so the before-button target is exactly what the memory held and what the memory rule computed. The recorded subgoal at that step contradicts the other three 'before' episodes in this minibatch, where the recorded drop goes to the placement preceding the press, and matches instead what an 'after' goal would ask for. No rule that fits the other episodes can also produce that answer, so the request is not passed on; the before/after distinction added above is drawn from the 'after' episode, not from this one.

history.critique:
refused
  One step reported that goal_target was wrong. The goal asked for the green cube on the target used right before the button press. In that demonstration the green cube was carried to the far-left target, released there with the cube resting within a few pixels of it, and it still lay on that same target in the frames immediately before the gripper closed and pressed the button; after the press it was moved to a different target and then put away. The annotator prompt, the policy prompt for memory, and the policy's own first-step computation all produced that far-left target, and the policy chose B: drop onto it. The recorded subgoal instead points at a third target that the goal cube never touched at any point in the demonstration, neither before nor after the press. The policy's proposed fix (take the nearest release before the press whose cube lies within 8 px of a target, and verify the cube rests there just before the press) gives exactly the value already written, so it would not change the outcome. In the other four episodes of this minibatch, both 'before' and 'after' goals, the same rule yields the target the recorded subgoal points at, with the recorded point within 1-2 px of the stored goal_target. The recorded label at this step therefore cannot be reached from the demonstration by any rule that also fits the other episodes, and I am treating it as noise in the recording rather than a defect in the documents. No change to any of the three documents is passed on.

applied.refused: The report asks for no change, and I commit none. The single failed step is a 'before' goal whose recorded drop points at a target the goal cube never touched in the demonstration, neither before nor after the press; the annotator prompt, the policy memory instruction, and the policy's own first-step computation all agree on the far-left target and the other four episodes of this round (both 'before' and 'after') confirm the rule within 1-2 px. Round 1 also refused one 'before' step whose label pointed at the after-press target. The two stray labels do not even disagree with the rule in the same direction (one names the after target, the other a never-used target), so no single rule reaches both while still fitting the nine conforming episodes across the two rounds; adding an exception for either would only break the episodes the documents already settle. The policy's proposed fix (nearest pre-press release within 8 px of a target, verified by the cube resting there just before the press) is already what the rule computes and would not change the value, so it is not added as redundant text. The documents stand as committed after round 1.

fields.name: goal_target
fields.description: If the memory carried in holds a value, copy it unchanged. If it is empty (first step, demonstration shown): read the goal instruction and note whether it says 'before' or 'after' the button was pressed. In the demonstration steps find the press frame: the first frame with fingers 0% open and height under 0.05, gripper over the button. A release is a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to 88% or more while height is under 0.05. For 'before', take the last release earlier than the press frame; for 'after', take the first release later than the press frame (do not take the later put-away release, where the cube ends more than 8 px from any target). The goal cube's [y, x] in that release frame is the placement point. Among the target entries listed in the execution scene at the bottom of this step, write the [y, x] of the one nearest that point. e.g. [86, 100]
fields.annotation: The [y, x] of the target the goal instruction names: the one the demonstration placed the goal cube on right before the button press if the goal says 'before', or right after it if the goal says 'after'. Found by reading the whole demonstration. The press frame is the first demonstration frame where the fingers go to 0% open with height under 0.05 and the gripper over the button. A release is a frame where the fingers widen from ~46% to 88% or more with height under 0.05. If the goal says 'before', take the last release earlier than the press frame; if it says 'after', take the first release later than the press frame (a later put-away release, where the cube ends more than 8 px from every target, is ignored). The goal cube's position in that release frame is the placement point; the field holds the [y, x] of the target entry nearest that point as listed in the scene at the start of execution. Written at the first decision step and never changed afterwards. e.g. [86, 100]

variables.policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal names one cube color (red, blue or green); call it the goal cube. The goal also says whether the wanted target is the one used 'before' or 'after' the button press; honour that word when computing goal_target. Never choose C (press the button): the button press in the video is only a marker telling you which target to use. Rules, applied in whatever situation you stand in: 1. Start of episode (memory empty, goal_target unknown, gripper raised out of frame, fingers 100% open): read the goal for 'before' or 'after', compute goal_target from the demonstration as the memory instruction says, then choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at the goal cube's current position in the execution scene. e.g. A: pick up the cube at [84, 122]. 2. Cube in hand (the scene at this decision step shows fingers about 46% open with the gripper raised, height near 0.15, after the execution steps showed it descend to the cube and close; the cube may or may not be reported as 'held in the gripper', trust the finger opening) and cube_placed is 'no': choose B: drop onto, pointing at the target entry in the current scene nearest to goal_target (targets wobble a few pixels; use the current listed position, e.g. B: drop onto at [87, 101]). If no listed target is within 10 pixels of goal_target (it may be hidden), point at goal_target itself. 3. Cube not in hand (fingers 100% open) and cube_placed is 'no' and goal_target is known: the pick failed or was never done; choose A: pick up the cube at the goal cube's current position. 4. cube_placed is 'yes' and the goal cube rests on goal_target: the task is complete; if a subgoal is still required, choose B: drop onto the same target again only if the cube is in hand, otherwise choose A: pick up the goal cube (keeps the loop safe). Never press the button. 5. Any situation not covered: if fingers are about 46% open and the gripper is raised, treat the cube as held and apply rule 2; otherwise apply rule 3. Never choose C.
